title: Rust reading: 1,000,000 rows, inline strings
dataset: 10 columns per row: integers, strings (one unique per row), floats, a date/time and a boolean; 1M rows with inline strings (49 MB file)
method: examples/read_bench.rs. The file is written by Hypaxel and read cell by cell, with a checksum over all values that every reader must match. Each run is in its own process; best of three.
notes: About a quarter of the time is inflate. Common cell shapes and plain shared string items are matched in a single pass over the buffer; anything else goes through the general pull parser.
Row buffers are reused, so reading allocates nothing per cell.
reproduce:
cargo run --release -p hypaxel --example read_bench -- generate data.xlsx 1000000 inline
cargo run --release -p hypaxel --example read_bench -- hypaxel data.xlsx     # or calamine, calamine-stream
